definition: Bubblegum Crash (バブルガムクラッシュ!, Baburugamu Kurasshu!) is a 1991 OVA anime series produced by Artmic and Artland.
details: It is the sequel to the 1987 OVA series Bubblegum Crisis, taking place a year after the series. The Knight Sabers seem to be finished, as each of its members except Nene Romanova have seemingly drifted off to pursue their own goals. But at the same time, a recent string of robberies, murders, and Boomer malfunctions begin to occur. Knight Sabers' leader Sylia Stingray is then forced to recruit Nene and the other members back together. The group tries to find out who or what is behind the recent string of crimes which are somehow related to the creation of an advanced artificial intelligence. After the split between Artmic and Youmex, Artmic proceeded to make Bubblegum Crash on their own, which ran three OVA episodes and is conjectured that it was a shortened version of how Bubblegum Crisis was to end. Youmex then sued Artmic, cutting the series short and tying the franchise up in legal issues until the late 1990s, when Artmic went bankrupt and Youmex was absorbed into Toshiba EMI. Upon release, the series received mixed reviews from fans and critics.

explainer.lead: Bubblegum Crash is a three-episode animated science-fiction mystery from 1991, not an AI technique. Its plot connects crimes and robot malfunctions to the creation of an advanced artificial intelligence, using AI as the mystery’s central unknown.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a team of heroes has split up, but strange robot breakdowns and crimes make them work together again. As they follow the clues, they discover that the trouble may be connected to someone creating a very advanced computer mind. The story is a three-part sequel to Bubblegum Crisis.
tiers.practitioner: There is no model here to implement, train, or evaluate; the advanced AI has no specified technical design. Engineers can treat the story as a fictional prompt for incident analysis: correlate malfunctions with other events, investigate possible causes, and avoid assuming that “AI” explains behavior without a mechanism.
tiers.paperLevel: There is no formal AI definition or formula: “advanced artificial intelligence” is an unspecified plot element rather than a described computational system. Bubblegum Crash follows the 1987 OVA Bubblegum Crisis and is set one year later. Its three-episode run was cut short after Youmex sued Artmic.

explainer.example: A robbery occurs while Boomers are also malfunctioning. Rather than treating these as unrelated incidents, the reunited Knight Sabers investigate them as parts of one pattern, eventually looking for a link to the creation of an advanced AI.

explainer.whyItMatters: Its mystery offers a fictional way to think about machine malfunctions, hidden causes, and responsibility for advanced systems. The series also illustrates how business disputes can shape a creative work: litigation cut it short and left the franchise tied up in legal issues until the late 1990s.
misconceptions: It is an anime series, not an AI algorithm or model.
It is the sequel to Bubblegum Crisis, not the original 1987 series.
Its advanced AI is not given a detailed technical design.
